newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - June 6.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION ON JULY 14

The country's 11th presidential election will be held on July 14. The notification will be issued on Monday and the candidates can file their papers until June 23. This time a nomination needs the endorsement of 50 proposers and as many seconders instead of 10 each. As per a presidential ordinance, a candidate will also have to deposit 15,000 rupees as security instead of 2,500 rupees. Announcing the presidential election schedule, the chief election commissioner said scrutiny of nominations will take place on June 24 and the last date for the withdrawal of candidature will be June 26. Counting of votes, if required, take place on July 17.
Indian Express
LALOO FACES CONTEMPT PLEA

The Janata Dal party's assistant returning officer, B.K. Prasad, moved the Delhi High Court challenging party chief Laloo Yadav's decision to call the national executive of the party on June 8. Prasad sought the initiation of contempt proceedings against Laloo for allegedly violating the Delhi High Court's May 31 order restraining him from interfering in the party polls. The contempt petition, accompanied by an application for an interim stay of the executive meeting, was filed in court on Thursday afternoon.
The Economic Times
RESERVE BANK PUTS BIG NONBANKING FIRMS ON WATCHLIST

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has decided to monitor about a dozen of the biggest non-banking financial companies (NBFCs). The companies will be tracked on a weekly basis by the RBI to ensure that their operations follow prescribed procedures. These NBFCs are on the watch list because they have a large depositor base and substantial liabilities. The NBFCs on the watch list include Lloyds Finance, ITC Classic, Peerless General Finance and Investment Company, the Ceat Finance, HB Leasing and Portfolio, IFB Finance, and Jenson & Nicholson Finance.
HUDCO'S RUPEE BONDS FOR FOREIGN INVESTORS

The Housing and Urban Development Corporation (Hudco) is set to launch a one billion-rupee bond scheme meant exclusively for overseas investors. Hudco will also launch a non-resident Indian deposit scheme to mobilise about 2.5 billion rupees in 1997/98 (April-March). The Reserve Bank of India has already given an in-principle approval for the scheme. Both the schemes are expected to come into operation by mid 1997/98. The amount will be raised through private placement at certain coupon rates. The bonds will place no ceiling for individual investment. If the scheme is successful, Hudco may go in for larger placement in this year itself.
INDUSTRIAL DEVELOPMENT BANK TO RAISE 140 BLN RUPEES

The Industrial Development Bank (IDBI) has drawn up plans to raise 140 billion rupees from the domestic and international markets in 1997/98 (April-March). Of this, 110 billion rupees will be in rupee borrowings and the remaining through foreign currency borrowings. The target is 18.64 percent higher than that of last year. The bank has already sought government permission to raise $850 million in external commercial borrowings this year. On the rupee front, IDBI has internally set a target of 25 billion rupees to be raised through retail deposits. Other rupee-raising resources include private placements and public issue of bonds.
UK FIRM TOLD TO INJECT INDIAN EQUITY INTO JOINT VENTURE

The government is treating non-resident Indian (NRI) equity on a par with foreign equity in the non-banking financial sector and is differentiating it from resident equity. While considering the proposal of BZW Worldwide Holdings of UK to set up a joint venture to provide a comprehensive range of non-banking financial services with a company owned by NRI BZW employees, the Foreign Investment Promotion Board has said in view of the guidelines on the NBFCs with a 75 percent foreign equity amounting to $5 million, it is mandatory for the companies to bring in 25 percent resident equity. BZW wants to hold a 75 percent stake in the proposed venture.
Financial Express
ITC GOES FOR INDUSTRIAL BANK LOAN TO CHECKMATE BAT

The ITC has approached the Industrial Development Bank (IDBI) for a three billion rupee loan. The loan has been sought to fund the tobacco division expansion project. But sources said a major reason is to ensure continuity of the financial institutions' nominees on the company's board. The move will checkmate the possibility of ITC's parent BAT acquiring an upper hand in the management of the company in which the stakes held by foreign institutional investors and global depository receipts are believed to have exceeded 10 percent. BAT has a 32.7 percent stake.
UNITED AIRLINES EYES INDIAN FIRMS

United Airlines (UA) is holding preliminary talks with Indian companies for a possible tie-up. After its tie-up with Thai Airways International, UA is looking for an alliance partner in Asia and talks were being held with both Indian and Chinese companies. UA's senior vice president said they are having very preliminary level discussions with some Indian companies for a possible tie-up, but there is nothing concrete yet. The airliner at present has daily flights connecting the Delhi-London and Delhi-Hong Kong sectors as its Indian operations.
FOREIGN BANKS TO UNDERWRITE RELIANCE'S LOAN

The Bank of America, ABN Amro Bank, Bankers Trust and Toronto Dominion have agreed to fully underwrite and syndicate Reliance Petroleum's (RPL's) upcoming $300 million 10-year foreign currency loan. The four banks have underwritten the entire $300 million syndicated loan of RPL to the extent of $75 million each. The RPL forex loan is priced at 200 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate (Libor), which is 140 basis points higher than the price of the 10-year facility being raised by the public sector Steel Authority of India. The 10-year loan is the Reliance group's first major borrowing from the international market for 1997/98 (April-March).
Business Standard
CRB CAPITAL PRESIDENT, 4 DIRECTORS ARRESTED

The Central Bureau of Investigation arrested six persons in connection with the 12-billion rupee CRB Capital group case. The investigating agency seized documents worth billions of rupees and other papers which could throw light on the extent of the alleged financial irregularities. Those who were arrested include the president of CRB Capital Markets, four of its directors and a relative and close associate of the group's chairman C.R. Bhansali. The seizures included the company's shares worth 1.3 billion rupees, three cheques worth 70 million rupees and shares of other companies worth another 70 million rupees.
COGENTRIX TO DILUTE STAKE IN MANGALORE POWER COMPANY

U.S.-based power major Cogentrix Energy Inc is seeking a buyer for its equity in the Mangalore Power Company, which is putting up a 40 billion rupee, 1,000 megawatt power project in Karnataka state. Cogentrix holds 60 percent of the Mangalore Power Company's equity. The other 40 percent is held by China Light and Power International. Cogentrix gave no reason for the sudden decision to dilute its stake in the controversial project. But the new company brass is said to be lukewarm to the project which has been hanging fire for the last five years.
ELECTRONICS, SOFTWARE EXPORTS POST 90 BLN RUPEES

The Electronics and Computer Software Export Promotion Council notched up exports worth 90.23 billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March). This was up 42 percent from last year and represented 42 percent growth in export performance in rupee terms and 34 percent in dollar terms over the previous year. The contribution of the electronics and software sector to the country's total exports increased from 3.2 per cent in 1992/93 to 7.7 percent in 1996/97. The export of electronic hardware has risen by 33 percent from 24 billion to 31.85 billion rupees. Telecom and related services showed an increase of 30 percent in revenue.
POWER PACT WITH NEPAL TO BENEFIT MULTINATIONALS

Two treaties signed in Kathmandu by India and Nepal open the way for private companies, including multinationals, to take part in bilateral trade in the power and air traffic sectors. This could be the first step towards opening up the economic borders within South Asia. The power pact could hold the key to solving India's power problems. Nepal has an estimated potential to generate 83,000 megawatts of hydroelectric power. It now generates only 245 megawatts. Companies like the Enron Power Corporation will now be able to generate power in Nepal and sell it in India. The treaty allows any party in Nepal or India to trade power.
The Observer
OVER THE COUNTER EXCHANGE TO TRADE GOVERNMENT SECURITIES

The Over-the-Counter Exchange of India (OTCEI) has received the Reserve Bank of India's assent for trading in government securities. It is now awaiting the Finance Ministry's approval and is confident of getting it soon. Currently, trading in government securities is permitted only at the national bourse. The move is expected to bring depth and liquidity into secondary market trading in government securities. It is also expected to add to the liquidity of these securities by extending its reach to 26 cities, where the OTCEI has centres. OTCEI will also expose the instruments to a large section of retail investors in the non-metros.
FULL TAX RELIEF FOR PRIVATE ROADWAYS PLAYERS

The government has decided to give 100 percent income tax exemption on profits for the first five years to operators of road infrastructure facilities. Thereafter, they will get 30 percent income tax exemption on profits for another five years. The minister of Surface Transport said it has been decided to permit the National Highway Authority to provide capital grants up to 40 percent of the project cost for build operate transfer projects. Laws will be amended to include acquisition of land for housing and other development activities to be treated as acquisition for public purposes.
INDUSTRIAL DEVELOPMENT BANK'S NET UP BY 13.6 PCT

The Industrial Development Bank of India has announced a 13.6 percent higher profit after tax and increased the dividend rate to 35 percent for 1996/79 (April-March). Net profit was 11.44 billion rupees. Loan disbursals rose by 6.9 percent to reach 114.35 billion rupees despite the industrial slowdown. This stood at 106.93 billion rupees in 1995/96. The project loan disbursements went up by 54.7 percent which indicated progress in implementation of projects, sanctioned assistance in previous years.
